sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Love and will are still a finite existence, whereas true self-nullification is the service of accepting the yoke, like a servant with no will of his own, and this aspect of nullification is inherited from the Patriarchs who were the Merkavah.

translations.translation: And it is known,
that love is the love and will of the person
(the lover),
and therefore,
even when his love and will is that the Supernal will be fulfilled,
nevertheless,
the essential concept of love and will is an existence.
And the true concept of nullification is in the service of accepting the yoke,
which is like a servant who has no desires whatsoever,
and everything he does is because of the yoke of the master that is upon him,
by virtue of which he is compelled to fulfill the will of the master.
And it can be said,
that since the nullification of the chariot to the rider is not from the will of the chariot
(that it wants to be nullified to the rider and be a chariot for him),
but rather from the rider,
therefore, in the inheritance from the Patriarchs, who are the Merkavah, there is also included in concealment the nullification of accepting the yoke.
[And one may note from the saying of our sages, of blessed memory,
"At the time that Israel preceded 'we will do' to 'we will hear'... who revealed this secret to My children?" And it is explained in Chassidus
that this precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear"
[that in the nullification of accepting the yoke itself, there is a most elevated nullification,
nullification to the Master of Will]
is through the revelation of the hidden love,
a secret.
And it can be said,
that the connection of the hidden love
(existence)
to the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear"
(nullification of accepting the yoke),
is,
that the hidden love is an inheritance from the Patriarchs, who are the Merkavah].
And from this it is understood,
that the nullification drawn down to Israel at the giving of the Torah
(after they preceded "we will do" to "we will hear")
is a nullification more elevated even than the nullification of the Merkavah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The "Great Matter" is the Work of the Chariot, which elevates from the limited level of "Man" to the unlimited level of "Not-Man," specifically through the Chariot of the Patriarchs in Atzilus.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that it is stated in the Gemara,
"They said about Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai that he did not leave out anything great or anything small—
'a great matter' is the Work of the Chariot, 'a small matter' is the discussions of Abaye and Rava."
And it is explained in the Maamar,
that the reason the Work of the Chariot is called a "great matter" is,
that through the chariot,
the person riding upon the chariot reaches a place he cannot reach on his own,
and likewise is it in the Supernal Chariot,
that the Chayos bear the Throne
and the Man upon the Throne
to the level of "Not-Man."
And the main elevation to the level of "Not-Man" is through the Chariot of the Patriarchs
(the Patriarchs, they are the Merkavah),
the Chariot of Atzilus.
For the elevation of the level of "Man" to the level of "Not-Man" that is through the Chariot of BY"A is that the Man upon the Throne
(the Man of BY"A)
is elevated to a level that is a level of "Not-Man" relative to the Man of BY"A,
and through the Chariot of the Patriarchs,
the Chariot of Atzilus,
there is an elevation of the level of Man of Atzilus to the level of "Not-Man" that is above Atzilus,
Arich.
And this is that the Work of the Chariot is called a "great matter,"
for Man,
Zeir Anpin,
is a level of smallness and contraction,
and through the Chariot he is elevated to the level of Arich,
Great.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The discussions of Abaye and Rava are called a "small matter" because the laws of the Torah are clothed in small, limited things, and the Torah itself is a parable and garment for the Ein Sof, which is a small thing relative to the inner essence of Torah to be revealed in the future.

translations.translation: And the reason that the discussions of Abaye and Rava are called a "small matter"
(even though they are the essence of the Oral Torah)
is,
that the laws of the Torah are clothed in small things.
For in addition to the fact that the mitzvos are clothed in physical things,
each mitzvah has many particular laws,
for the concept of division
(particulars)
is contraction and limitation,
smallness.
[And based on this,
the difference between the Work of the Chariot and the discussions of Abaye and Rava is from one extreme to the other.
For the concept of the Chariot is the departure from the level of limitation
(Man)
to the level of without limitation
(Not-Man)
— a great matter
(for the true concept of greatness is in something that is not limited),
and in the discussions of Abaye and Rava it is the opposite,
the clothing of the Supernal Will,
which is without limit,
in limited things — a small matter].
And the Maamar continues with another reason for this, that the discussions of Abaye and Rava are called a "small matter,"
because the Torah of now is a small thing relative to the inner aspect of the Torah that will be revealed in the future.
And also because the Torah is a parable and garment for the Ein Sof that is clothed within it.
Therefore the Torah is called "the parable of the Ancient One,"
for it is a parable and garment for the level of the "Ancient One of the World."
And a parable relative to the thing being parabled is a small thing.
